data.one_liner: A library for communication with CQRS-compatible backends using queries and commands.
data.what_it_does: Provides a client and abstractions to send queries, commands, and operations to a CQRS-compatible backend. It handles request execution and returns structured results including command successes and validation failures.
use_when: Your backend architecture follows the CQRS pattern.
You need to send strongly typed queries and commands over HTTP.
avoid_when: Your backend uses standard REST or GraphQL without CQRS.
You are looking for a general-purpose HTTP client.
strengths: Strongly typed query and command contracts.
Built-in handling for validation errors and command execution states.
No-throw guarantee API returning results explicitly.
weaknesses: Requires a specifically CQRS-compatible backend architecture.
Limited to HTTP transport using the provided client.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting up an HTTP client and a base API Uri, then instantiating the Cqrs class.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer making standard raw HTTP requests instead of a structured CQRS architecture.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a fully-featured general HTTP client with interceptors and advanced request management.
